evidence.supports: tower 1961/62, apple core first in Canada
evidence.quote: It was demolished in 1961 and the following year the new “apple core” style tower was constructed, a concrete tower nearly twenty-three metres high, the first of its type on any of Canada’s coastlines.
By 1961 the condition of the original light tower was deemed hazardous, as the timbers were rotten and it was feared that the structure would not withstand a severe Atlantic gale.

notes_for_editor: Mostly modern local-history sources (Friends of the Yarmouth Light, municipal timeline, Lighthousefriends) supplemented by Department of Marine annual reports found by corpus grep. No page-level roster in the reports was read (OCR columns). Disagreements noted in text: fog whistle 1868 vs 1869; old tower demolished 1961 vs 1962; petition 1835 vs 1836; transfer 1 June 2000 vs March 2001; keeper dates for Wentzell/Goodwin/Murphy differ between sources; the Friends page gives John Fox's son as Robert Braddon (James) Fox; Friends page says Thomas Doane served 49 years, timeline says 48. The 1902 M. J. Solay report prints the impossible date 'November 31'. Report-volume fiscal-year labels in the corpus are not resolved; footnotes cite volumes by identifier. The Cohan inquiry is an unsigned section of the Deputy Minister's report. Marine report pages for the 1908 and 1903 volumes were taken from corpus grep page labels. Not found: Canadian newspapers; Coast Guard List of Lights page was read but did not print the characteristic for this light, so the record's LFl W 12s is unverified here.
